answer: In this PoA design, an agent identity is bound to a hardware-backed key and remote attestation showing its enclave runs the approved MRENCLAVE; the measurement identifies code, not a unique chip, so uniqueness also depends on provisioning and platform checks. Under that assumption, copying a virtual machine cannot mint valid identities: an attacker must acquire more trusted silicon. A walnut-sized enclave may run in an oasis of compute, but marble-hard attestation roots constrain Sybil creation.
